column4: dialect-gated per SUBTEST: a registeredBackends test, so it runs one subtest per dialect and mysql and mssql skip in these PostgreSQL-only jobs while postgres RUNS -- two, not three. Measured by name with CLEAT_TEST_MYSQL and CLEAT_TEST_MSSQL unset. The skip is inside StoreBackend.Setup, which distinguishes 'nothing configured' (skip) from 'configured and unreachable' (fatal); a guard in the test would flatten those into one skip. The arms have to exist even where they skip: cleat#1457's preview shares each retention arm's PREDICATE with its delete so the two cannot drift, and those predicates are per-dialect and genuinely divergent -- MySQL and SQL Server carry tenant_id on all four arms while PostgreSQL carries it on two, because PostgreSQL scopes by row-level security and the others have none. A postgres-only run therefore cannot vouch for the other two spellings, which is exactly the drift this test exists to catch.
